notes: Editable data layer for the static model in schema.json. Every node and relationship has exactly one slot here - an empty or placeholder 'select' means it has not been mapped to Finacle yet. Nothing is hardcoded in Java; the engine reads schema.json (shape) + this file (queries). SELECTs may contain a single '?' which the engine binds to the row limit.

nodes.label: Account
nodes.select:
SELECT g.foracid         AS accountnum,
       g.acid            AS acid,
       g.cif_id          AS cifid,
       g.sol_id          AS solid,
       g.schm_code       AS schemecode,
       g.schm_type       AS schemetype,
       g.acct_name       AS accountname,
       g.acct_short_name AS shortname,
       g.acct_crncy_code AS currency,
       g.clr_bal_amt     AS balance,
       g.acct_opn_date   AS openeddate,
       g.acct_ownership  AS ownership,
       g.acct_cls_flg    AS closedflag,
       s.acct_status     AS status
FROM   tbaadm.gam g
LEFT JOIN tbaadm.smt s ON s.bank_id = g.bank_id AND s.acid = g.acid
WHERE  g.bank_id = '01'
  AND  g.del_flg = 'N'
  AND  g.entity_cre_flg = 'Y'
  AND  ROWNUM <= ?
nodes.notes: Grounded in STR/SAR/GraphSelectors: tbaadm.gam g LEFT JOIN tbaadm.smt s. key = foracid (accountNumber); acid is the join id used by the transaction/relationship slots; cif_id links to Customer.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.select:
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT a.CIF_ID AS cifid,
         MAX(country)   AS country,
         MAX(c.NAME)    AS name,
         MAX(a.CIF_TYPE) AS ciftype,
         MAX(dob)       AS dob,
         MAX(solID)     AS solid,
         MAX(a.opendate) AS opendate
  FROM   custom.cif_acct_data_aml a
  LEFT JOIN custom.CIF_DATA_aml c ON c.CIF_ID = a.CIF_ID
  GROUP BY a.CIF_ID
)
WHERE ROWNUM <= ?
nodes.notes: Source = SIMBA.ACCOUNT_DATA a LEFT JOIN SIMBA.CIF_DATA c (domain input). key = CIF_ID (customerId). NAME is a single field -> stored as 'name' (the model's firstName/lastName are not derivable from it). CIF_TYPE carried as cifType.

nodes.label: Transaction
nodes.select:
SELECT h.tran_id   AS tranid,
       h.tran_date AS trandate,
       h.sol_id    AS solid,
       h.pstd_flg  AS postedflag,
acid as acid,
       h.tran_amt          AS amount,
       COUNT(*)    AS legcount
FROM   custom.ctd_dtd_acli_view h
WHERE  h.bank_id = '01'
  AND  h.pstd_flg = 'Y'
GROUP BY h.tran_id, h.tran_date, h.sol_id, h.pstd_flg,acid,h.tran_amt
nodes.notes: PARENT level: one node per BUSINESS transaction (tran_id + tran_date) = 2,264. GROUP BY guarantees exactly one row per transaction, so legs can never collapse a parent or overwrite it with last-leg-wins. The individual double-entry postings live in the 'transactionEntry' slot (keyed + part_tran_srl_num). Fraud queries MUST count/sum THESE nodes, never the entries.

nodes.label: TransactionEntry
nodes.select:
SELECT   h.tran_id           AS tranid,
       h.tran_date         AS trandate,
       h.acid              AS acid,
       h.tran_amt          AS amount,
       h.rcre_Time as input_time,
       h.del_flg as del_flg ,
       h.tran_crncy_code   AS currency,
       h.tran_type         AS trantype,
       h.tran_sub_type     AS transubtype,
       h.part_tran_type    AS parttrantype,
       h.PART_TRAN_SRL_NUM as parttransrlnum,
h.REF_NUM as refnum,
h.tran_particular   AS particulars,
       h.tran_particular_2 AS particulars2,
       h.tran_rmks         AS remarks,
       h.instrmnt_num      AS instrumentnumber,
       h.pstd_flg          AS postedflag,
       h.sol_id            AS solid,
       h.rate              AS exchangerate,
       h.ref_crncy_code    AS refcurrency
FROM   custom.ctd_dtd_acli_view h
WHERE  h.bank_id = '01'
nodes.notes: CHILD level: one node per double-entry POSTING/leg = 8,753. Key is (tran_id + tran_date + part_tran_srl_num), verified unique within a transaction in Oracle. Every posted column is stored for traceability. NEVER count these for AML velocity/amount - they are postings, not business transactions.
nodes.cypher:
UNWIND $rows AS r
WITH r WHERE r.tranid IS NOT NULL AND r.trandate IS NOT NULL AND r.amount IS NOT NULL AND r.acid IS NOT NULL AND r.parttransrlnum IS NOT NULL
MERGE (n:TransactionEntry {transactionId: toString(r.tranid), date: toString(r.trandate), amount: toString(r.amount), acid: toString(r.acid), parttransrlnum: toString(r.parttransrlnum)})
SET n.currency = r.currency
SET n.tranType = r.trantype
SET n.tranSubType = r.transubtype
SET n.partTranType = r.parttrantype
SET n.solId = r.solid
SET n.particulars = r.particulars
SET n.particulars2 = r.particulars2
SET n.remarks = r.remarks
SET n.postedFlag = r.postedflag
SET n.del_flg = r.del_flg
SET n.instrumentnumber = r.instrumentnumber
SET n.exchangerate = r.exchangerate
SET n.refcurrency = r.refcurrency
SET n.refnum = r.refnum
SET n.input_time = r.input_time

nodes.notes: Source = SIMBA.ACCOUNT_DATA + SIMBA.CITY (CITY_CODE resolved from CITY_NAME). key = addressLine1 + city (street + mandatory locality; postal code is optional in Kenya/EAC, country is a separate node via LOCATED_IN). relationships.select:
SELECT DISTINCT g.foracid AS accountnum, h.tran_id AS tranid, h.tran_date AS trandate
FROM   custom.ctd_dtd_acli_view h
JOIN   tbaadm.gam g ON g.acid = h.acid AND g.bank_id = h.bank_id AND g.del_flg = 'N'
WHERE  h.bank_id = '01'
  AND  h.pstd_flg = 'Y'
relationships.notes: Account -> Transaction, the ANALYTICAL edge fraud queries traverse. Endpoint key MUST match the Transaction node key (tran_id + tran_date) or the MATCH is ambiguous. DISTINCT because a transaction touches an account via several legs.

relationships.select:
SELECT DISTINCT h.tran_id AS tranid, h.tran_date AS trandate, h.part_tran_srl_num AS legsrl
FROM   custom.ctd_dtd_acli_view h
WHERE  h.bank_id = '01'
  AND  h.pstd_flg = 'Y'
relationships.notes: Parent -> leg. This is what lets a drill-down go transaction -> its double-entry postings. Both endpoints must exist: run the 'transaction' and 'transactionentry' nodes FIRST.

relationships.select:
SELECT DISTINCT h.tran_id AS tranid, h.tran_date AS trandate, h.part_tran_srl_num AS legsrl, g.foracid AS accountnum
FROM   custom.ctd_dtd_acli_view h
JOIN   tbaadm.gam g ON g.acid = h.acid AND g.bank_id = h.bank_id AND g.del_flg = 'N'
WHERE  h.bank_id = '01'
  AND  h.pstd_flg = 'Y'
relationships.notes: Which account each posting hits (the leg's acid resolved to the business account number). This is the true money-movement edge - use it for flow analysis; 'performs' is the same join rolled up to the transaction.

relationships.select:
-- PLACEHOLDER: destination account of the transaction
SELECT <tran_id> AS tranid, <dest_foracid> AS accountnum
FROM   <transaction_table>

relationships.notes: Destination/beneficiary account - still unresolved. Findings from STR/STAR: ctd_dtd_acli_view rows are single legs (part_tran_type 'C' = credit/beneficiary, 'D' = debit); the in-bank destination may be the sibling credit leg (same tran_id + tran_date), while external destinations come from clearing/messaging tables (SIMBA.CLEARINGAMLRP, SIMBA.CLEARINGAMLEFTRP, "CreditTransfer"@mariadb, APZTB_TRANSACTION_REQUESt@FCIXLINK, tbaadm.smh/cgm/pord/porh). Needs domain sign-off before a real SELECT.

relationships.select:
SELECT accounts.orgkey AS cifid, g.foracid AS accountnum
FROM   tbaadm.gam g
join crmuser.accounts
on orgkey = g.cif_id
WHERE  g.bank_id = '01'
  AND  g.entity_cre_flg = 'Y'
relationships.notes: Grounded: gam.cif_id -> Customer, gam.foracid -> Account. No role/since columns found in Finacle, so this relationship carries no properties.
relationships.cypher:
UNWIND $rows AS r
MATCH (a:Customer {customerId: toString(r.cifid)})
MATCH (b:Account {accountNumber: toString(r.accountnum)})
MERGE (a)-[rel:HAS_ACCOUNT]->(b)
SET rel.cifid = r.cifid
SET rel.accountnum = r.accountnum
